cli_cmd_push: Publish a blueprint markdown file into a project

skill_intro: The blueprint skill is the annotation side of this registry: it marks canonical patterns in your codebase with @Blueprint comments, indexes them, and nudges Claude Code to reuse them. Its index is what the CLI publishes here.
skill_source_link: Source and full reference on GitHub
skill_install_description: The installer copies the skill into .claude/skills/blueprint/ and records where it came from in a lockfile. It needs gh authenticated against an account with access to the repository; the skill itself is pure POSIX shell, with nothing to install at runtime.
skill_install_gotcha_pin: A bare bundle name resolves to that bundle's latest release tag, but an explicit resource path does not. Set FOS_REF to pin a tag, or install the quality bundle, which contains the skill.
skill_install_gotcha_readme_label: The installer strips README.md from the installed copy.
skill_install_gotcha_readme: SKILL.md ships with the normative annotation rules; the long-form reference stays
skill_annotate_description: An exemplar is the canonical example of a pattern. It carries a comment block directly above its declaration, in whatever line-comment syntax the language uses.
skill_annotate_gotchas_title: Three rules that bite in practice
skill_annotate_gotcha_comment_label: Never put @BlueprintGlobs in a block comment.
skill_annotate_gotcha_comment: A glob containing two asterisks and a slash embeds a comment terminator, which closes the comment early and breaks the file. Use line comments whenever globs are present.
skill_annotate_gotcha_glob_label: Globs are relative to the repository root,
skill_annotate_gotcha_glob: the directory Claude Code runs in. In a monorepo the glob must carry the package prefix:
skill_annotate_gotcha_id: category-prefixed (controller-create, repository-search). Anything else is silently dropped from the index.
skill_index_description: The index comes in two files: a markdown one for humans, and a TSV twin that the hooks, the matcher and the CLI all read.
skill_index_commit_why: — on a fresh clone the hooks then work immediately.
skill_hooks_description: Without hooks the skill is a catalogue. With them, Claude Code reuses your blueprints by construction. Add this to the project's committed .claude/settings.json — pattern consistency is a team property.
skill_hooks_behaviour: The SessionStart hook injects the compact index once per session boot, and stays silent above 150 entries. The Write and Bash pairs notice a new file matching a blueprint's globs with no @FollowsBlueprint annotation and remind Claude which blueprint applies. Nothing is ever blocked, and existing files are never checked, so brownfield work stays noise-free.
skill_hooks_telemetry: The check hooks append one JSONL line per event to
skill_hooks_telemetry_merge: That file is committed, so it rides along in your commits. To make concurrent appends merge cleanly, add
skill_publish_description: Run the sync from the repository root: the index records exemplar locations relative to it, and the CLI reads those files to classify each blueprint.
skill_publish_slug: Each @Blueprint becomes a blueprint whose slug is its pattern id, so re-running sync updates in place and only creates a version when the content changed.
skill_publish_scope: Slugs are unique per project, so --project scopes the lookup: your form-field never collides with another project's.
skill_publish_techno: Technologies are detected from the exemplar's imports. When a wrapper hides the real dependency, split the index by path and pass --techno per subset; --layer overrides the fallback layer.
skill_publish_cli_hint: Need the CLI first, or the full list of flags?
skill_update_title: Keeping the skill up to date
skill_update_body: It prompts before overwriting .claude/skills/blueprint/ and refreshes the entry in the lockfile. The lockfile stores a hash of the installed files, so a diff against a release tells you whether the project has drifted locally.
